definition: Compliant means meeting the rules and willing to follow them.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word compliant. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know compliant should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The dairy kept its labels compliant with the new dating law, reprinting every carton a month before the deadline.

Cooperative bends less of your own will than compliant does — two teammates trading suggestions are cooperating as equals, rulebook or none, while compliant means a written code is met point by point.
Submissive goes further than compliant — compliant means following the written rules, while submissive means yielding your own will to another person's.

Dutiful people do what duty asks of them, with a note of moral seriousness — the dutiful nurse stays late because it is right. Compliant is cooler and more clerical: it means the written rules are met, and a form, a factory, or a filing can be compliant with no sense of duty at all.

Amenable describes an attitude: open to suggestion, easily persuaded to go along — an amenable colleague says yes before the plan is even finished. Compliant is about the rulebook, not the mood: a site or a filing is compliant when every written requirement is met, whatever anyone feels.
